root_cause.text: The RDS/IB send completion path in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` did not recognize masked atomic work request opcodes even though `rds_ib_xmit_atomic()` always submits atomic cmsgs with masked atomic opcodes, causing atomic completions to return `rm == NULL` while `send->s_op` remained set and later NULL-deref in `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP` to the atomic-op switch cases in `net/rds/ib_send.c`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that previously masked atomic completions “fell through to default and returned rm == NULL while send->s_op is left set,” after which `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` dereferenced `rm->m_final_op`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle masked atomic InfiniBand work request completions using the atomic unmap path.
intent_record.what: Two additional work request opcode cases, IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD and IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP, were added to the switch statement so they follow the same branch as the existing atomic opcodes and invoke the atomic unmap handling path.
intent_record.how: At runtime, completions for masked atomic InfiniBand send operations are now recognized as atomic requests and, when send->s_op is present, are associated with the containing rds_message and passed to rds_ib_send_unmap_atomic() instead of falling through to non-atomic handling.

grouping_result.intent: Handle masked atomic InfiniBand work request completions using the atomic unmap path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it updates send completion/unmap handling to recognize masked atomic work request opcodes and route them through the atomic unmap path, preventing the atomic completion mismatch that led to NULL dereference.

candidates.rationale: The switch only handled unmasked atomic opcodes. Because masked atomic work requests were submitted elsewhere, completions for those opcodes missed this atomic-unmap path and left send->s_op set, leading to later NULL handling issues.

This case list was incomplete: it recognized only standard compare-and-swap completions, not masked atomic compare-and-swap completions, which is the direct root cause of the wrong completion-path handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is part of the incomplete opcode switch handling in rds_ib_send_unmap_op(). The atomic completion path recognized only the unmasked compare-and-swap opcode, while transmitted atomic work requests used masked atomic opcodes. As a result, masked atomic completions failed to take the atomic unmap path, causing rm == NULL and leaving send->s_op set for a later NULL dereference.

This statement shows the switch handled only the unmasked fetch-and-add atomic opcode. Because masked atomic opcodes were not recognized alongside it, atomic completions submitted with masked opcodes bypassed the intended atomic unmap handling, which is the root cause of the later inconsistent state and NULL dereference.

Author: Andy Grover <andy.grover@oracle.com>

    RDS: Perform unmapping ops in stages
    
    Previously, RDS would wait until the final send WR had completed
    and then handle cleanup. With silent ops, we do not know

    handles any of these cases by keeping a pointer to the last

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows both the completion-side opcode dispatch in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` and the atomic transmit setup in `rds_ib_xmit_atomic()`, which are the relevant pieces for the stated root cause. The vulnerable construct is present in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` where the switch only recognizes `IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP` under the atomic cases: `case IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD:` and `case IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP:`. There is no handling for masked atomic opcodes. The root cause says atomic sends are submitted with masked atomic opcodes by `rds_ib_xmit_atomic()`, and in this commit that function sets up an atomic work request (`send->s_wr.wr.atomic.remote_addr = ...; send->s_wr.wr.atomic.rkey = ...;`) but does not add any completion-side recognition for masked atomic opcodes. As a result, if `send->s_wr.opcode` is a masked atomic opcode, execution falls into the `default:` case, prints `unexpected opcode`, leaves `rm` as `NULL`, and returns it. The CQ handler then does `rm = rds_ib_send_unmap_op(ic, send, wc.status);` followed by `if (&send->s_op == &rm->m_final_op)`, which dereferences `rm` even though `rm` may be `NULL`. Also, because the atomic case was not matched, `send->s_op` is not cleared in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()`. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present, and the fix is not yet present because masked atomic opcodes are still absent from the switch handling.
